findings.title: A failed ps lookup now fails the whole measurement
findings.description: `executable_table()` calls `run(["ps", "-axo", "pid=,comm="])` with the default `check=True`, so any non-zero `ps` exit raises `StepFailed`. `wait_for_quiet_machine()` calls it on every poll, including polls where the machine is already quiet and the hint is never used, so the error propagates to `main()`, which reports `PERF_CHECK_RESULT` with status `fail`.

evidence.explanation: The PR says the diagnostic list never changes the go/no-go decision, but a diagnostic-only `ps` call can now turn a quiet, measurable machine into a hard `fail` verdict. The sibling `process_table()` uses `check=False` and tolerates failure, so the two calls in the same loop handle the same kind of failure in opposite ways.

findings.title: Failed ps lookup goes unlogged
findings.description: `executable_table()` runs `ps` with `check=False` and ignores the return code, so a failed `ps -axo pid=,comm=` yields an empty table. `competing_processes` and `busiest_processes` then fall back to `command.split()[0]` for every process without logging anything, truncating paths with spaces such as `/Users/me/My Tools/scons` and letting a competing build go undetected.

`executable_table()` runs `ps -axo pid=,comm=` with `check=False` and returns stdout without checking the return code, so a failed call yields an empty table.
`busiest_processes` uses the same `executables.get(pid) or command.split()[0]` fallback, so its hint also shows a truncated name such as `Google` for a spaced app path when the pid is missing.
The new spaced-path test always supplies the executable table, so the fallback branch that the commit message is meant to replace is not exercised by any test.

evidence.explanation: `executable_table` ignores the return code, so an empty result is indistinguishable from a successful run with no processes. `competing_processes` (line 527) and `busiest_processes` (line 564) then fall back to `command.split()[0]` with no log, reproducing the space-in-path miss the PR claims to fix whenever `ps -o comm=` fails or the table is incomplete. Nothing reports that the fallback was used, so the gate can measure beside a competing build with no trace; the likelihood is low because `ps` normally succeeds, so this is informational.

findings.title: Busy hint can name an argument as the app
findings.description: `process_name()` searches the full `ps` command for an `.app/` path, so it can return a bundle name from an argument instead of the executable’s name. When a busy tool such as `find` or `rsync` receives an app-bundle path as an argument, that name reaches the quiet-machine wait log if idle is low and no competitor is found.

findings.title: Busiest-process hint vanishes for moderate CPU users
findings.description: `busiest_processes()` reuses `COMPETING_CPU` (20%) as its minimum CPU floor, so only processes at or above 20% are listed. When idle CPU is below the limit because load is spread across one or more processes each under 20%, `busiest` is empty, the `and busiest` guard in `load_gate()` drops the hint, and the wait log still shows only the bare `cpu N% idle, below 50%` line this PR was meant to explain.

COMPETING = re.compile(r"(^|/)(godot|Godot|scons|clang\+\+|clang|cc1plus|ld|ld64)(\s|$)")
COMPETING_CPU = 20.0

def busiest_processes(ps_output: str, mine: int, limit: int = 3,
                      min_cpu: float = COMPETING_CPU) -> list[str]:
    """The busiest processes that are not ours, of any kind, busiest first. They name what is
    using the CPU when the idle figure is low but no known competitor is running."""
    found = sorted(busy_processes(ps_output, mine, min_cpu), key=lambda p: (-p[1], p[0]))
    return [f"{pid} {executable.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]} {cpu:.0f}% cpu"
            for pid, cpu, executable in found[:limit]]

evidence.explanation: The skill defines the quiet-machine gate as waiting while less than half the CPU is idle or while another heavy process runs, and this PR's new diagnostic reports that wait. `COMPETING_CPU` (line 62) is 20%, and `busiest_processes` (lines 526-535) passes it as the minimum to `busy_processes`, so diffuse load yields an empty list and `load_gate` (lines 535-546) adds no explanation. The PR's stated purpose is to name what uses the CPU when no competitor does, but the reused competitor threshold hides exactly the low-to-mid CPU consumers that can sum to a low idle figure.

findings.title: Process names with spaces are cut to one word
findings.description: `busy_processes()` takes `command.split()[0]` as the executable, so a macOS app path containing spaces is truncated at the first space before `rsplit('/')` runs. The hint then reports a fragment such as `Google` or `Visual` instead of the real application name, which is the only detail the new message exists to provide.
